chapter: Closing: recent career, family and travel
title: Seventies work: Cookery, Kool Festival and New Orleans plans
summary: He played the Cookery, Cockatoo, Pace College and the Carnegie Chamber recital with a good Times review, and plans a New Orleans trip.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So in the last few years you've been more or less freelancing around New York...
We're just going to sum up some of the things that you've been doing in the last few years.

Well, in the Seventies, the early Seventies, I went on the road with the singer Tom Jones. After that I played several clubs here and stayed around New York. Right up to this time, I've played most of the spots. I've been at the Cookery; Barney Josephson, who used to own the old Cafe Society, that's his place. And a few clubs in the Village. I occasionally go on the road.
Of course, supper clubs is a... There's a place called the Cockatoo.

That's on First Avenue in the Seventies. That's what they call the strip, the strip on the East Side of New York. The East Village and then the strip -- the strip would be First Avenue, Second Avenue and Third Avenue.
I've played at Pace College several times, you know. And then I played the Kool Jazz Festival, at Carnegie Chamber...
The chamber at Carnegie being the small hall.
You had a very good review in the Times for that recital.
Yes, I did. I think Dorothy Donegan and I had about the best review, thanks to the very wonderful John Wilson, one of the knowledgeable...
And I've been playing around with Bill Simon of the Reader's Digest and George Simon, the Jazz critic. And I do occasional records with various groups.
I intend to go to New Orleans this year.
To the Festival? I think it's on now...
The Festival will be in '84, or the next years to come, so I'm going down there to prepare.
